title: the birth
hook: in Kamsa's prison, a child is quietly moved from one mother to another, and the gods come to sing to an unborn baby

segments.voice: Yesterday the birth began at a wedding: a voice from the sky, Kamsa's sword, and Vasudeva's promise, kept. Your line was a promise made at sword point. Did a calm word help anywhere yesterday? Day eight hundred eighty.

The Bhagavata doesn't linger on it, and neither will we. In the prison, Kamsa kills Devaki's children as they are born. The text says that when six had died, a seventh child began to grow in her. And this time, something is done in secret. The Lord, the Bhagavata says, calls on his own power of illusion, Yogamaya, and gives her a task. A child is in danger. Move him. Today, the hidden work that happens before the birth.
screen: `A PRISON IN MATHURA.` → `THE SEVENTH CHILD.` → `"MOVE HIM."`

segments.voice: Yogamaya draws the seventh child out of Devaki's womb and places him in the womb of Rohini, another wife of Vasudeva, who is living safely in Gokula, a village of cowherds across the river. In the prison, people say Devaki has miscarried. In Gokula, the child grows in secret. The Bhagavata names him from that night: he will be called Sankarshana, the one who was drawn out. Later he is known as Balarama, Krishna's older brother. So the first rescue in this story is quiet and invisible. Then the Lord himself enters Devaki. The text says he first enters Vasudeva's mind, and from there passes into Devaki, and she begins to shine. The prison can't hold the light. Kamsa sees her glowing and understands: this is the one. But he can't bring himself to kill a pregnant woman, his own cousin, and so he waits, and the waiting turns into obsession. The Bhagavata says that sitting, lying down, eating, walking, Kamsa saw that child everywhere. His fear made him think of the Lord constantly. And while Kamsa paces, the gods come. Brahma, Shiva and the others arrive and stand in the cell to sing praise to the child inside Devaki. Do not be afraid, mother, they tell her. The one in your womb has come to protect the world. It's a strange and tender scene: a dark cell, a frightened mother, a jailer outside, and inside it the whole sky gathered around someone who hasn't been born yet.
screen: `THE SEVENTH CHILD IS MOVED` · `SANKARSHANA: DRAWN OUT` · `KAMSA SEES HIM EVERYWHERE` · then, large: `THE GODS SING TO THE UNBORN CHILD`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your breath find its own pace. Think of something good that is growing slowly in your life and isn't visible yet. A friendship. A skill. A healing. A child on the way. Breathe in, and let yourself notice it, without hurrying it. Breathe out, and let go of the urge to check on it. The gods in the story came just to stand near something that hadn't arrived. You can do the same. If you pray, you can hold it in your prayer. The bell holds the time.
The birth. Before it happens, a brother is moved to safety, a mother begins to shine, and the gods come to sing.
Your line: the gods come to sing. Today, notice one good thing that is still growing, and leave it alone to grow. Day eight hundred eighty.

howItsDone: The prayer the gods offer to the child in Devaki's womb, told in the Bhagavata Purana's tenth book, is heard when the Bhagavata is recited, and Balarama is honored alongside Krishna in temples and festivals.

fork.setup: you're Kamsa. your prisoner is glowing, and you're sure the child that will kill you is inside her. what do you do?
options: hold back, and wait for the birth.
fork.reveal: he won't kill a pregnant woman, so he waits, and his fear makes him see the child in everything he does.

original.note: sankarshana: the Bhagavata gives Balarama this name because he was drawn from one womb to another.

trapdoor: what you thought: Krishna's older brother was simply born before him.
what it means: in the story, Balarama is moved from Devaki's womb to Rohini's, to keep him from Kamsa.
what a scholar hears: the Bhagavata itself explains his name, Sankarshana, from that drawing out.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.2: the six children killed, Yogamaya and the transfer of the seventh child to Rohini, the name Sankarshana, the Lord entering Vasudeva and Devaki, Kamsa's fear, the prayer of the gods

notes: All paraphrase. The count 'when six had died' follows Bhagavata 10.2 (hatesu satsu balesu); confirm.
Confirm that the text says the people spoke of a miscarriage, and that it gives the name Sankarshana for being drawn from the womb (10.2.13).

Confirm the sequence: the Lord enters Vasudeva's mind, then Devaki; Devaki's radiance; Kamsa refrains from killing a pregnant woman and thinks of Hari while sitting, lying, eating and walking (10.2.24).
The gods named as Brahma and Shiva with others; confirm. Their words to Devaki are a gloss.
The gods' prayer is known as the garbha-stuti; howItsDone describes its recitation only generally.
Editor pass: cut 'unseen by the guards', which the cited chapter does not state.
